description: We are a team of young innovators using Earth and space data to identify locations that simulate Moon and Mars environments. Our goal is to compare environmental conditions and help test equipment for future space exploration..
summary:
SPACEANALOG is an interactive bilingual (Arabic and English) platform that uses Earth locations like Egypt’s Western Desert, Atacama Desert, and Haughton Crater to simulate Moon and Mars environments.

It uses NASA data, 3D visualizations, and AI tools to compare temperature, pressure, gravity, and soil conditions. It also helps scientists plan missions and allows students to learn through a Gemini AI voice assistant.

Most importantly, it supports blind and visually impaired people through screen readers, keyboard navigation, and audio feedback.
details: SPACEANALOG is an interactive, bilingual (Arabic and English) web platform designed to identify and characterize terrestrial analog environments on Earth that simulate conditions on the Moon and Mars. Testing space hardware and training astronauts off-world is costly and risky; SPACEANALOG addresses this challenge by connecting Earth’s extreme analog sites—such as Egypt’s Western Desert, the Atacama Desert, and Haughton Crater—with lunar and Martian terrains using open NASA planetary and Earth observation data. Scientists and mission planners can utilize the Smart Mission Matcher, interactive 3D terrain visualizations, and Side-by-Side Scientific Comparison tools to evaluate temperature, atmospheric pressure, gravity, and soil metrics. Meanwhile, students and the general public benefit from an age-adaptive Gemini AI Flight Director voice assistant that simplifies complex concepts. Crucially, SPACEANALOG champions radical inclusivity by integrating full ARIA screen-reader support, keyboard navigation, and automatic audio feedback, empowering blind and visually impaired explorers to discover space science independently from Earth.
